correctness.rationale: For c_n=(alpha)_n/n!, Stirling yields square-sum cutoff alpha=1/2. When alpha<1/2, symbol phi_alpha belongs to H², has strictly positive real part and is outer, so its polynomial multiples are dense and ordinary-formal zero row output implies f=0. When alpha>=1/2, finite Vandermonde correction on M+1 distinct phase frequencies cancels first M rows with arbitrarily small l² tail norm. Abel sums and dominated convergence in l¹ weights control ALL partial sums inside correction blocks, not merely endpoints. Consequently dense ordinary-series kernel and full-product graph closure follow. Poisson recovery shows no Herglotz atoms as alpha<1. Essential scope separates maximal formal transform from closed Smirnov Toeplitz.
